answer: Randomized epoch re-check: a verifiable delay function produces a seed that forces a lagoon of identities to submit fresh proofs of past actions. Each proof must mirror the exact prior log, and because the seed is published only after the epoch closes, an attacker cannot precompute which action to forge. A fake identity costs a sonnet of independent proof computations per round, and any missing proof triggers immediate deletion, so expected total loss scales linearly with sybil count times per-check expense.
